source: NCERT Class X, Science, Ch. 9 (Light – Reflection and Refraction).

sections.heading: 1. Reflection and Spherical Mirrors
points: **Laws of reflection:** angle of incidence = angle of reflection; incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in one plane.
**Spherical mirrors:** **concave** (converging) and **convex** (diverging).
Terms: **pole (P), centre of curvature (C), radius of curvature (R), principal focus (F), focal length (f)**; **R = 2f**.

sections.heading: 2. Images by Spherical Mirrors
points: **Concave mirror** — image varies with object position (real/inverted or virtual/erect/magnified when object within focus). Uses: **torches, headlights, shaving mirrors, solar furnaces, dentists**.
**Convex mirror** — always **virtual, erect, diminished**; wide field of view. Uses: **rear-view mirrors** of vehicles.
**Mirror formula:** 1/v + 1/u = 1/f; **magnification m = -v/u = h'/h**.
**Sign convention (New Cartesian):** distances measured from pole; along incident light = +, against = −.

sections.heading: 3. Refraction of Light
points: **Refraction** — bending of light when it passes from one medium to another (due to change in speed).
Ray bends **towards the normal** entering a **denser** medium, **away** entering a **rarer** medium.
**Laws of refraction (Snell's law):** n = sin i / sin r = constant for a pair of media.
**Refractive index** = speed of light in vacuum ÷ speed in medium; higher index = **optically denser**.
Examples: a pencil looks bent in water; a pool looks shallower; twinkling of stars.

sections.heading: 4. Refraction by Lenses
points: **Convex (converging) lens** — converges light; **concave (diverging) lens** — diverges.
**Convex lens** images: vary with object distance (real/inverted, or virtual/erect/magnified as a **magnifying glass**).
**Concave lens** — always virtual, erect, diminished.
**Lens formula:** 1/v − 1/u = 1/f; **magnification m = v/u**.
**Power of a lens** P = 1/f (in metres), unit **dioptre (D)**; convex = +, concave = −.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: R = 2f; concave = converging, convex = diverging mirror.
Convex mirror image = always virtual, erect, diminished (rear-view mirror).
Mirror formula 1/v+1/u=1/f; lens formula 1/v−1/u=1/f.
Refractive index = c(vacuum)/v(medium); denser medium = higher index.
Power P = 1/f (metres), unit dioptre; convex +, concave −.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Convex mirror** always gives a **virtual, erect, diminished** image (used as rear-view mirror).
**Concave mirror** is used in **headlights/torches** (converging).
Light bends **towards the normal** entering a **denser** medium.
**Power of a lens** is in **dioptre** (P = 1/f in metres); concave lens power is **negative**.
